aspects.says: SelectDestination's BIN table is configuration, tried from the range written with the most digits; a Mastercard table written as 5 declines 2-series cards.
basis: section:5.2 The BIN Table Is Configuration, and the Most Specific Range Wins

aspects.says: Each participant element is its own instance with its own configuration; static configuration lets the last element configured decide for all.
basis: section:5.4 Each `<participant>` Element Is Its Own Instance, With Its Own Configuration

aspects.says: A selector's select names groups that the TransactionManager runs, in the order named, right after the selector and before the rest of the chain.
basis: section:5.1 A Selector Names a Group, and the Group Runs Where the Selector Stands

aspects.says: A selector name with no group adds nothing, with only a WARNING in the transaction event, which debug false removes; the request goes on unchecked.
basis: section:5.3 A Name With No Group Behind It Runs Nothing

aspects.says: A missing or misspelt required property is refused in setConfiguration, so the deploy fails instead of the check passing everything.
basis: section:5.4 Each `<participant>` Element Is Its Own Instance, With Its Own Configuration

aspects.says: Only a request the network received can need a reversal: a silent network does, a decline or a down link doesn't.
basis: section:5.6 A Network That Doesn't Answer Has Not Declined

aspects.says: With call-selector-on-abort, select is called on the abort path without the selector's prepare, and only the abort participants of the selected group run.
basis: section:5.1 A Selector Names a Group, and the Group Runs Where the Selector Stands
aspects.reason: seen only in the transaction trail, which the lesson shows; no answer a terminal receives differs, so neither a test nor a scenario question would check more than a reading of the trail

aspects.says: CheckFields records failures in the Result and votes ABORTED without a response, extra fields fail by default, and an abort participant has to turn the failure into an answer.
basis: section:5.5 A Stock Participant Reports a Failure, and an Abort Participant Has to Answer It

aspects.says: With continuations, QueryHost resumes a timed-out transaction as prepared with no response; a participant after it must fail the transaction so the terminal gets 91.
basis: section:5.6 A Network That Doesn't Answer Has Not Declined
